decision: Equal-unit, equal-minor-group, equal-prefix5-group and employment weights are compared over one matched universe of complete cells. The original 923-code scores are reported separately and again re-ranked inside the matched universe.
rationale: A change of weights must not be confounded with a change of universe. The controlled comparison changes weights only. The second comparison isolates the effect of the universe.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when the OEWS year or the O*NET release changes.

decision: Primary rule soc: one unit per BLS-defined SOC occupation inside a cell, represented by its .00 O*NET-SOC profile. Units in a cell are distinct SOC occupations, so they are disjoint worker groups and the min/max bounds keep the disjoint-cell interpretation: they hold for any nonnegative split of the cell employment among its SOC occupations (bound_type disjoint_allocation_bound). Nested detailed codes are never substituted for a missing .00 profile.
rationale: The O*NET-SOC taxonomy treats the .00 code as the SOC-level occupation. It does not say that detailed specialties partition that occupation, so a specialty split would impose an allocation no source supports.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if O*NET publishes how detailed codes partition a SOC occupation.

decision: Sensitivity rule code is labeled synthetic profile reweighting. Every O*NET-SOC code in a cell, including detailed codes nested under a .00 parent, is an equal-weight alternative. It is not a disjoint worker allocation. Its min/max envelope (bound_type profile_envelope) is a profile-allocation sensitivity, not a sharp bound over mutually exclusive worker groups.
rationale: A .00 description and its detailed descriptions overlap in the workers they describe. Equal weights over all codes therefore mix overlapping groups. The envelope shows how far the choice of profile moves prevalence.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the taxonomy states how detailed codes relate to the .00 parent.

decision: A two-stage split, equal across SOC occupations in a cell and then equal across the codes of each, is reported under the code rule only. It is blank under the soc rule, where every SOC occupation has one unit and the two stages coincide.
rationale: It checks whether the split between SOC occupations and codes drives the code-rule result.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the code rule changes.

decision: The cell inventory is built from the full Occupation Data roster, the OEWS cell list and the bridge. It is not inferred from the retained activity rows. Each OEWS detailed row is one cell and is counted once.
rationale: Inference from retained rows would hide SOC occupations without an activity profile and could count combined-code employment twice.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the roster or the cell list changes.

decision: Allocation units are defined per rule before any bound is computed. Cells are disjoint OEWS detailed rows, so employment is counted once. Under the soc rule the units in a cell are distinct SOC occupations. Under the code rule the units are exclusive profile alternatives that can overlap in the workers they describe. Unit identifiers are unique across cells.
rationale: The roster has more titles than data-level codes, and parent and detailed codes coexist. A bound over undefined units would have no interpretation.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a rule is added.

decision: Each cell is complete, partial, no_profile or unmatched. Only complete cells enter the headline estimate. Partially observed cells are reported separately from cells with no profile. Coverage is shown against the official all-occupations total and against the returned unsuppressed panel.
rationale: Suppressed employment dropped before panel construction is invisible to coverage measured against the returned panel alone.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if OEWS changes its suppression rules.

decision: Cells with a SOC occupation that lacks a profiled .00 code are counted in the incomplete, partial and no_profile coverage scopes, and in the inventory columns n_socs_without_00_profile and n_nested_profiled_unused_soc_rule. The soc rule does not fill them with specialties.
rationale: Substituting a specialty profile would silently change the estimand. The count shows how much employment the choice affects.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a defensible partition of SOC occupations into specialties appears.

decision: Cells that hold an All Other SOC occupation with nested detailed codes are disclosed in the coverage scope cells_with_all_other_soc_with_nested_detail under both rules.
rationale: The .00 description of such an occupation has no activity profile while its specialties do. Treating the specialties as the occupation is a mapping choice, so the employment is shown and not allocated.
revisit_trigger: Revisit with the cells_without_00_profile decision.

decision: The official all-occupations total exceeds the sum of detailed rows by a small residual. It is reported as official_not_returned and is not folded into any bound.
rationale: The files used do not explain the residual, so no cause is asserted.
revisit_trigger: Close the gap if BLS documents the residual.

decision: Exact bounds: lower counts a cell only when every unit links the activity, and upper counts it when any unit links it. Wide bounds also let the employment of the incomplete cells in the returned panel either link or not link the activity. They leave out the 13,890 workers of the official total that no cell returns. Under the soc rule they are allocation bounds over disjoint worker groups. Under the code rule the same columns are the profile envelope of emp_rule_code, a profile-allocation sensitivity and not a sharp bound. They are not confidence intervals and do not bound actual worker activity use.
rationale: Allocation bounds show where unknown within-cell splits matter and where they cannot, for example when all units agree.
revisit_trigger: Revisit with the allocation rules.

decision: The union upper allocation scenario is the employment_upper column. It is a labeled bound under the soc rule, the top of the profile envelope under the code rule, and never the headline estimate.
rationale: A union assigns all cell employment to a link that may describe only a small specialty.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Equal-unit and equal-minor-group prevalence are not allocations of cell employment, so they can fall outside the employment bounds. The share outside is reported as description only.
rationale: They answer a different question, namely how widely a link appears among descriptions, not among workers.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: equal_minor_group uses the first four characters of the SOC code, which is a true SOC minor group. equal_prefix5_group uses the first five characters and reproduces the article grouping. Both are reported under their own names.
rationale: The article calls the five-character prefix a minor group, but a SOC minor group has four characters.
revisit_trigger: Revisit after the article terminology is corrected.

decision: The correction of the article wording belongs to the coordinator. This batch adds the true minor-group scheme and does not edit the article or the existing snapshot.
rationale: Article text is outside this batch.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Every published OEWS combination code and its constituent SOC occupations come from the BLS Occupation Definitions workbook and are compared with the package constituent list. Only detailed OEWS rows are used. In the May 2025 file every combination code appears as a detailed row, so the public panel builder drops none.
rationale: Some combination codes also appear as broad rows with the same employment. Using every row would count that employment twice.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when a new OEWS year changes the combination codes.

decision: The package constituent list names SOC 25-9041 as part of combination 25-9045. The 2025 BLS definition does not include it and the 30.3 roster has no such code. The difference is recorded in the combination audit and in the accounting rows, and R/ is not edited.
rationale: The extra code has no effect on the inventory. Editing the package is outside this batch.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when the package constituent list is next updated.

decision: No change to the public OEWS panel builder is warranted for May 2025. The raw national file was checked directly and not only through fixtures.
rationale: All combination codes are detailed rows in the raw file, and the builder keeps detailed rows only.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a later OEWS year publishes a combination code only on a non-detailed row.

decision: One national, cross-industry May 2025 panel. The area, industry and ownership columns of the workbook are asserted to be uniform and counted in employment-accounting.csv.
rationale: The package reader drops these columns, so the scope is checked on the workbook itself.
revisit_trigger: Revisit before any state, metro or industry analysis.

decision: Employment describes OEWS coverage: nonfarm wage and salary workers, excluding the self-employed. Military O*NET-SOC codes have no OEWS cell and no activity profile.
rationale: The BLS Technical Notes define the survey population.
revisit_trigger: Revisit with a new OEWS release.

decision: The employment-weighted information budget is not implemented.
rationale: The review makes it optional and places it after the prevalence extension. It would replace log2(N) with H(O). The existing helper hardcodes equal weights, so passing employment-weighted scores to it would not implement the change. Bits across priors are not evidence that work became more or less distinctive.
revisit_trigger: Revisit after the prevalence extension is reviewed and a use for the bits is stated. Test against H(O) if implemented.

decision: Employment-weighted skill distributions and thresholds are not computed.
rationale: The review says they can follow the allocation audit. The skills universe needs its own cell-completeness audit first.
revisit_trigger: Revisit after the skills universe is accepted.

decision: State, metro and industry OEWS panels are not built.
rationale: They change the cell inventory and the suppression pattern, and need their own coverage audit.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when a sub-national question is posed.

decision: OEWS sampling error is not propagated. The relative standard error of each cell is carried in the cell inventory.
rationale: Propagating it through ranks and bounds needs a variance model that this batch does not specify. The bounds are allocation bounds, not confidence intervals.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a variance model is chosen.

decision: A Core-only task restriction is not run for the employment-weighted activity prevalence. The employment outputs keep the article baseline, which counts an occupation as linked to an activity through any task.
rationale: The article states that a literal Core-only restriction would shrink the universe to 893 occupations, which is a different universe and not a robustness pass. It lists Core-only filtering among checks a substantive claim should survive. Skills ratings do not use task links.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the article adopts the restriction.

decision: Essential and Transferable skills are separate blocks and Importance and Level are separate scales. Blocks are es_im, es_lv, ts_im and ts_lv. No distance concatenates domains or scales.
rationale: Concatenating domains adds an avoidable weighting decision.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: The primary distance is the mean over elements of the absolute rating gap divided by the scale range, one block at a time. It treats equal numeric gaps as comparable across elements within a scale. That is an assumption.
rationale: Absolute ratings preserve overall requirement differences. Row-normalizing would make (2, 2) and (4, 4) identical.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the Level anchors show that element gaps are not comparable.

decision: Element-specific Level example anchors at values 2, 4 and 6 and item-level gaps for the nearest, median and farthest pair in each block ship beside the distances.
rationale: A common numeric range does not make different skill levels substantively identical.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: A row-normalized total-variation distance is reported as a secondary view of requirement mix, as nearest-set overlap and distance rank correlation only.
rationale: The review allows a normalized composition as a secondary view for questions about the mix of requirements.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: The distribution of every element rating over the primary universe is reported: mean, spread, percentiles, share at the scale minimum and Not Relevant count.
rationale: The review asks for distributions and interpretable profile differences before any league table.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Share at or above a threshold uses the inequality >=. Thresholds come from the scale descriptions: Importance category labels at 2, 3 and 4 with a grid that stops at 4.5, and Level example anchors at 2, 4 and 6. Other values are labeled grid points. Not Relevant is shown as recorded and as excluded, and Level shares are also shown with Not Relevant ratings floored to 0. Integer Importance thresholds do not mean that most analysts chose that category, because values are means over eight analysts.
rationale: Thresholds need scale descriptions, a declared inequality and a stated Not Relevant treatment, with sensitivity across defensible cutoffs.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the scale descriptions change.

decision: No skills rarity league table is published.
rationale: The review says distributions and interpretable profile differences are more informative first, and thresholds must be shown to change the leaders before any ranking.
revisit_trigger: Revisit after threshold sensitivity of the leaders is shown.

decision: Presence-based IDF on every positive rating is not used.
rationale: It discards the level variation that the ratings carry.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Rater count, standard error, Recommend Suppress, Not Relevant and the Level auto-zero rule are audited and counted. The rule sets Level to 0 when an analyst rates Importance as 1. Nothing is repaired. No significance claim and no joint confidence interval is made.
rationale: Marginal standard errors without covariance cannot give joint intervals.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: The primary universe holds the DWA occupations that are complete in all four blocks and carry no Recommend Suppress flag. The complete pool without that exclusion is a sensitivity. Attrition by reason is disclosed in skills-common-universe.csv and skills-provenance.csv.
rationale: A fixed universe keeps every block comparable and lets the parent compare activity, skills and software neighbors on exactly the same codes. Recommended-suppressed ratings are not published as primary eligible measurements.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if O*NET changes the suppression rule.

decision: Not Relevant ratings are audited and kept with their recorded values in the primary distance. They are not excluded for being flagged. A floor sensitivity sets Level to 0 where Not Relevant is Y.
rationale: Not Relevant is not independent of Importance, and flagged values already sit near the floor.
revisit_trigger: Revisit with the audit.

decision: Pairwise-exclusion distances that drop missing elements per pair are not used.
rationale: They break the fixed support that makes neighbors comparable across blocks and domains.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: A rank-percentile-by-element distance on the fixed universe is compared with the primary distance by nearest-set overlap at k of 1, 5 and 10 and by distance rank correlation. No significance is claimed. The absolute primary distances and item-level gaps are retained.
rationale: Equal scale intervals and cross-element Level gaps are assumptions. This is a diagnostic, not a change of estimand.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the primary distance changes.

decision: Directed nearest neighbors are kept through k of 10 with every tie at the cutoff retained. Distances come from exact integer sums and are rounded to 8 decimals.
rationale: Retained ties make the nearest set well defined, and rounding removes floating-point noise.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Neighbors recomputed over the complete pool, with primary-universe queries, show how much the Recommend Suppress exclusion moves nearest sets.
rationale: The exclusion is a design choice, so its effect is disclosed.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: No information-loss budget is built for rated skills.
rationale: Averaging ratings is not the same operation as merging DWA probability mass. A synthetic draw proportional to ratings would impose a new interpretation of ratings as probability mass. The review says to defer it.
revisit_trigger: Revisit only with a stated probability interpretation.

decision: No composite or combined distance across domains or scales is computed, and no substantive measure is exported.
rationale: Combining blocks adds a weighting decision that the data do not settle.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: No education or experience comparison is built.
rationale: If added later it is a separate credential-requirement comparison, not a component of a combined score.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when a credential question is posed.

decision: The coordinator computes DWA and software neighbors on exactly the primary skills universe, compares overlaps at k of 1, 5 and 10, and inspects pairs close on activities but far on skills. This batch supplies skills-common-universe.csv, skills-nearest-neighbors.csv and the domain-agnostic neighbor helper.
rationale: Each domain keeps its native distance. Disagreements describe requirements from different sides and do not establish switching costs or worker transitions.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: The software companion and any employment weighting of software belong to the coordinator. Employment weighting of software follows only after its own coverage audit.
rationale: The review orders the batches this way.
revisit_trigger: None.

decision: Raw inputs are pinned by SHA-256 and are not bundled: the O*NET 30.3 text archive, the May 2025 national OEWS ZIP and the BLS occupation definitions workbook. The scripts read local paths, assert the checksums and never download.
rationale: Checksums let a reader confirm that the derived tables came from the stated bytes.
revisit_trigger: Revisit when an input changes.

decision: BLS returns HTTP 403 to scripted clients such as curl and a web fetch tool. A fetch of each source URL from inside a browser page returned the pinned bytes. The national ZIP is linked from the OEWS tables page. The definitions workbook is not linked from the tables, structure or technical notes pages and was verified only by fetching its direct URL.
rationale: The access path is recorded instead of assumed.
revisit_trigger: Close the gap if BLS allows scripted access or links the workbook.

decision: The README names BLS as the source of the employment totals and the occupation definitions. BLS states that everything it publishes is in the public domain except previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations, and asks users to cite BLS as the source. The statement was read on the BLS Copyright Information page in a browser.
rationale: Attribution follows the request that BLS makes on its own page.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if BLS changes https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm.

decision: No field-descriptions workbook ships in the May 2025 ZIPs. The column layout was verified from the Technical Notes, the Occupation Definitions workbook and the workbook headers.
rationale: The layout cannot be checked against a BLS field dictionary for this year.
revisit_trigger: Close the gap if BLS publishes one.

decision: The OEWS Survey Methods document was not read for this batch. Population scope comes from the Technical Notes page.
rationale: This is a non-blocking verification gap.
revisit_trigger: Close the gap by reading the methods document.

decision: Helpers are nonexported and sourced from inst/article-helpers. There are no new exports, no change to R/ or NAMESPACE, and no new dependency.
rationale: The batch adds research choices for the article, not package API.
revisit_trigger: Revisit if a measure is proposed for export.

decision: Article text, NEWS, docs, vignettes, pkgdown configuration and the existing occupational-distinctiveness snapshot are not touched in this batch.
rationale: The coordinator owns them.
revisit_trigger: None.
